status: Implemented and verified in source; not packaged or published
tested_platforms: Ubuntu under WSL: Python 3.12, portable test subset
features: Saved FlowNotes with distinct step IDs referencing existing nodes or suborbitals
Draft editor, concept search, reordering, relinking, labelled connections and explicit starting step
Manual branch choices, terminal connections, loops and Previous following the actual visit trail
Read-only structured study reader with canonical notes, additional records, concept links and recall prompts
Independent native directional arrows, shared concept highlights and repeated occurrence badges
Canonical note editing, repairable missing concepts and atomic save failure recovery
Flow records retained by JSON exports, backups, design changes and saved-state history
Compass, retractable layer navigation and stable atlas labels preserved
data_preservation: Flow references and arrows do not duplicate concepts, move coordinates, create spatial adjacency or increase heat
Study traversal and camera/filter navigation do not write atlas content or history revisions
Leaving a flow restores camera, representation, filters, orbit focus and unsaved inspector drafts
Opening an older schema-10 atlas/history does not create a false content revision
GUI and runtime checks use disposable atlases rather than the user's saved atlas
limitations: Published 0.9.3 installers do not include FlowNotes or read format 11
The Ubuntu system Python lacks Tkinter; the full Linux source suite and GUI were not verified for this change
No package, installer, update handoff or release was produced or tested for this change
Branching is manually authored and traversed, not a process simulation
Automatic progression, recall-answer reveals and a standalone comparative study-note view remain future work
